target_note: Asset-side baseline: Blender 5.2.1; documentation baseline: Blender 5.2 LTS Manual. Engine examples are version-stated documentation reads, not a production engine target and not runtime verification.

sources.title: Armature Modifier
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Armature modifier purpose, vertex groups, bone envelopes, multi-modifier behavior, parenting tip
supports: Armature modifier deforms vertices using vertex groups or envelopes
Skinning is distinct from object/bone parenting
Multiple armature modifiers can be mixed rather than chained
limits: Does not document game collision, WPO, or engine export behavior
Page text read via public search result, not a local Blender run

sources.title: Armature Skinning Introduction and Armature Deform Parenting
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Skinning introduction; Armature Deform parenting; automatic weights and caveats
supports: Parenting objects to bones moves them but does not deform vertices
Armature Deform parenting creates and sets up an Armature modifier
Automatic weights can overlap and require manual correction
limits: Does not establish a universal bone count or weight limit
Parenting plus modifier is not by itself a double-transform claim

sources.title: Armature Structure and Bone Chains
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Bone chains, connected versus offset parenting, ramified chains, root/tip terminology
supports: Bone chains can branch
Child bones may be parented but not connected
A parent bone can be part of multiple chains
limits: No vegetation-specific or gameplay-specific guidance
No claim that naming or hierarchy alone determines runtime behavior

sources.title: Bendy Bones (B-Bones)
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: B-Bone purpose, segments, curve handles, roll, vertex mapping, keying set
supports: B-Bones replace long chains of small rigid bones with a curved evaluation
More segments improve smoothness but increase pose cost
Straight and Curved vertex mapping have different cost/quality
limits: B-Bone evaluation is not documented as a portable engine runtime format
No vegetation-specific parameters or budgets

sources.title: Spline IK
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Setup, chain length, curve target, roll, offset, length/thickness modes, optimal bone length, hooks
supports: Spline IK aligns a connected bone chain to a curve and is suitable for ropes
Y Scale Mode controls whether the chain stretches, uses pre-IK scaling, or neither
Roughly equal bone lengths and control points every few bones are recommended
limits: No guarantee of length preservation in all modes
Constraint evaluation must be baked or converted for non-Blender consumers

sources.title: Hook Modifier
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Hook purpose, object/vertex group/strength, modifier-stack warning, falloff
supports: Hooks can deform meshes, curves, and lattices from another object
Hook assignment stores original indices and must precede generative modifiers
limits: No engine export guarantee
No branch or vine-specific workflow

sources.title: Bake Action
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Bake Action section: final motion, visual keying, clear constraints, frame step, channels
supports: Bake Action computes final motion including constraints/drivers into per-frame keys
Visual Keying and Clear Constraints are available
Baking is a way to turn evaluated rig behavior into explicit animation
limits: Baking does not make unsupported deformation models portable
No performance or engine-import claim

sources.title: Curve Geometry
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Offset/extrude, taper, bevel depth/resolution/caps, custom profile, tilt
supports: Curves can generate ribbons or tubes with controlled resolution and caps
Taper and point radius control thickness along a spline
limits: Curve data is an authoring representation, not a universal engine runtime asset
No vegetation-specific wind behavior

sources.title: Unreal Engine Material Properties - World Position Offset
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: World Position Offset maximum displacement, bounds extension, clamping artifacts, culling
supports: WPO can push rendered geometry outside static bounds and require max-displacement/bounds handling
A zero max displacement does not extend culling bounds
Clamping WPO can trade popping for flattened/hitching motion
limits: Documents rendering/culling, not collision or physics following WPO
Version is a documentation example, not the chosen project engine

sources.title: Set Bounds Scale
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: Purpose: frustum-culling bounds scale, useful for WorldPositionOffset
supports: Bounds scale is a separate rendering/culling control
WPO users may need explicit bounds expansion
limits: No cost-free bounds setting; larger bounds can hurt performance/shadows
No collision guarantee

sources.title: Animation to Texture Data Asset and Bake API
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: VAT data asset fields: vertex/bone mode, textures, sample rate, LODs, influences, UV channel
supports: VAT can store per-vertex positions/normals or per-bone transforms/weights
Static mesh LOD and skeletal mesh LOD are explicit bake inputs
Texture resolution, frame count, and bone influences are explicit costs
limits: Documented as an engine plugin workflow, not a Blender exporter or universal format
No runtime performance, collision, or dynamic branch interaction guarantee

sources.title: Per-Platform LODs
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: Ordered skeletal-mesh LODs, reduced geometry and bones, project-dependent step severity
supports: Higher LODs may reduce bone counts
LOD count and reduction severity are project-specific
limits: No universal screen-size or bone budget
No vegetation-specific LOD recipe

sources.title: Foliage Mode in Unreal Engine
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: Static Mesh Foliage instancing, Actor Foliage cost, cluster culling, per-instance fade, density scaling
supports: Static Mesh Foliage supports hardware instancing and single-draw-call clusters
Actor Foliage has normal Actor rendering cost
Per-instance fade and density scaling are explicit scalability tools
limits: Not evidence about skeletal trees or interactive collision
Cluster culling can cause abrupt group disappearance if not faded

sources.title: Pivot Painter Tool 1.0
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: Pivot/rotation data in vertex data, shader hierarchy, grass versus tree hierarchy, memory statement
supports: Per-pivot vertex data can drive hierarchical vegetation motion in a vertex shader
Trees benefit from hierarchy painting; grass should use per-object painting
Shader-driven motion avoids stored skeletal animation but is calculated on the fly
limits: UE 4.27-era page, not current engine or Blender functionality
Memory percentage is an example claim, not a budget for this project
No collision or interactive response

sources.title: tuxalin/vegetation-shader - Procedural Wind
sources.author: tuxalin (GitHub), with credited influences Tiago Sousa and Renaldas Zioma
sources.read_scope: README; branchWind.ush; foliageWind.ush; trunkWind.ush; repository file tree
supports: Separate trunk/foliage wind functions and LOD variants
Per-branch phase, branch attenuation, edge attenuation, branch weight
Mass/height/multi-frequency controls for trunk and foliage motion
Phase and amplitude can be encoded in texture or vertex color
limits: UE4 material project only; no current-engine verification
No collision or gameplay interaction
Uasset material graphs were not opened
No render or performance test

sources.title: pajama-studio/lowpoly-tree-generator
sources.author: pajama-studio / Rand Monster
sources.read_scope: README; src/rig.js; src/vines.js; repository file tree
supports: Optional rig separated from static generation
Bone chains derived from trunk/root/primary/secondary semantic curves
Branches parented at nearest point on the parent curve
Two-bone closest-segment weighting for low-poly trees
Level-specific wind strength and deterministic phase
Wind clips sampled for export
Vine recipe supports dual anchors and slack but read code generates static vine geometry
limits: Three.js/GLB implementation, not Blender or Unreal
Code was read, not executed; no GLB export or engine import
No LOD/collision/performance evidence
Nearest-point parenting and two-bone weights are untested on complex forks
